label: lem:cc_replacement
title: Strict improvement step, Bárány
statement:
Let \(T : \{0,\dots,d\} \to \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) be a family of
finite sets with \(0 \in \operatorname{conv}(T(i))\) for every \(i\).
Let \(p : \{0,\dots,d\} \to \mathbb{R}^d\) be a compatible rainbow
tuple (\(p(i) \in T(i)\) for every \(i\)), and let
\(q \in \operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{range} p)\) satisfy
\(q \neq 0\) and the KKT inequalities
\(\langle q, p(j) \rangle \ge \langle q, q \rangle\) for every \(j\).
Then there exists a compatible rainbow tuple \(p'\)
(\(p'(i) \in T(i)\) for every \(i\)) and a point
\(q' \in \operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{range} p')\) with
\(\|q'\| < \|q\|\).

\emph{Bárány's argument.} Since \(q \neq 0\) and
\(0 \in \operatorname{conv}(T(i))\), expanding \(0\) as a convex
combination of points in \(T(i)\) and pairing with \(q\) yields some
index \(i\) and point \(c \in T(i)\) with
\(\langle q, c \rangle \le 0\). Consider the augmented set
\(\operatorname{range} p \cup \{c\}\) of \(d+2\) points in
\(\mathbb{R}^d\); the closed half-space
\(\{x : \langle q, x \rangle \le \langle q, q \rangle\}\) is supported
by the hyperplane through \(q\) orthogonal to \(q\). The KKT
hypothesis places every \(p(j)\) on the far side, while \(c\)
satisfies the strict variant after a small perturbation along the
segment from \(p(i)\) to \(c\); in particular the segment intersects
the open ball of radius \(\|q\|\) about the origin, providing a point
\(q'' \in \operatorname{conv}\{p(i), c\}\) with \(\|q''\| < \|q\|\).
Replacing \(p(i)\) with \(c\) (or, by Carathéodory's theorem in
\(\mathbb{R}^d\), with a vertex of the augmented \(d+2\) point hull
that is redundant for representing \(q''\)) produces a compatible
rainbow tuple \(p'\) whose convex hull contains \(q''\), so
\(\|q''\| < \|q\|\) is the desired witness.
